name: TCA6408ARGTR
title: TCA6408A: 8-bit I2C/SMBus I/O expander, 1.65 V to 5.5 V, with interrupt, reset and level translation
summary: The TCA6408A gives an I2C or SMBus controller eight more general-purpose lines, P0 to P7, each set as input or output. Its I2C side runs from VCCI and its port from VCCP, each 1.65 V to 5.5 V, so it also shifts levels between the bus and the port. It has an open-drain interrupt that flags input changes, an active-low reset, a polarity inversion register and one address pin for two addresses (0x20, 0x21). It works at 100 kHz and 400 kHz, starts with every line an input, and comes in TSSOP-16, VQFN-16 and UQFN-16.
key_figures: 1 µA typ, VCCP 2.3 V to 3.6 V
6.5 µA typ, VCCP 2.3 V to 3.6 V, 400 kHz

notes: Every orderable number is the same TCA6408A die; they differ in package, reel and lead finish. Body sizes (nominal): TSSOP 5.00 mm × 4.40 mm, VQFN 3.00 mm × 3.00 mm, UQFN 2.60 mm × 1.80 mm.
An automotive-qualified (Q100) version, TCA6408A-Q1, also exists.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A 1.8 V controller reaches a port powered from VCCP over I2C. Four 10 kΩ resistors pull SCL, SDA, INT and RESET up to the 1.8 V rail, which also feeds VCCI and the controller. ADDR goes to ground, giving address 0100000. P0 reads an alarm line from another subsystem; P1 drives the enable of a switch between A and B. P2 to P4 read a keypad and carry 100 kΩ pull-ups to VCCP; P5 to P7 drive the keypad's other lines. The design example is VCCI 1.8 V, VCCP 5 V, 400 kHz.

operation.text: VCCI is tied to the supply of the I2C bus and sets the thresholds of SCL, SDA and RESET; VCCP supplies the device and sets the port levels. Each may be anything from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, so the part translates in either direction between 1.8, 2.5, 3.3 and 5 V systems.

Four 8-bit registers: Input Port, Output Port, Polarity Inversion and Configuration. All can be read back. After power-up or reset every line is an input, Output Port holds all ones, Polarity Inversion all zeros.
Shows the logic level present on every pin, inputs and outputs alike. It is read only; writing to it does nothing. To read it, first write the command byte 00 so the next read comes from it.
Sets the level driven on lines configured as outputs and has no effect on inputs. A read returns the flip-flop contents, not the level on the pin.
A 1 in a bit inverts the sense of the matching input as seen in the Input Port register; a 0 leaves it as it is.
A 1 makes the line an input with its driver off (high impedance); a 0 makes it an output.

Each line has a push-pull output stage of two FETs to VCCP and ground and an ESD diode to ground. As an input both FETs are off and the pin can be taken up to 5.5 V, above VCCP. As an output one of the two FETs is on; the outputs sink enough current to drive LEDs directly.

INT goes low, after tiv, when any line set as an input changes from the state last held in the Input Port register, on either edge. It clears when the input returns to its earlier state or when the port that caused it is read; the clear takes effect on the SCL rising edge of the ACK or NACK bit in a read, so an input change during that clock may be missed or show only as a brief pulse. A line set as output never interrupts. Traffic to other devices on the bus does not touch it. Turning an output into an input can raise a false interrupt if the pin level differs from the Input Port register. INT is open drain and is pulled up to VCCI or VCCP, whichever the receiving device runs from.

Holding RESET low for at least tW returns the registers and the I2C state machine to their defaults without removing VCCP, the same as a power-on reset. With RESET high the port can be changed by the controller or from outside. RESET needs a pull-up to VCCI when nothing drives it.

As VCCP rises from 0 V, the part stays in reset until VCCP reaches VPOR, then the registers and the bus logic start at their defaults. A new power-on reset needs VCCP taken back below VPORF and up again. Once both supplies are up and the reset has happened, the part answers on the bus at any time.

Bring VCCP up before VCCI so SDA cannot be held low. The reset release level differs depending on whether the supply came down to 0 V or only below the POR threshold. Glitch width and depth trade against each other, and bypass capacitance and source impedance change how a glitch is seen.
The 7-bit address is 010000 followed by the ADDR level: 0x20 with ADDR low, 0x21 with ADDR high, so two devices can share a bus. The eighth bit is R/W, 1 for a read and 0 for a write.

After the address is acknowledged in a write, the next byte is a command byte, kept in the control register, whose two low bits pick the register; the other six bits are 0. It is sent only in write transfers and stays set for later reads.

Standard-mode (100 kHz) and Fast-mode (400 kHz) I2C, with Schmitt-trigger inputs and input filtering on both bus lines. A write is START, address with R/W = 0, command byte, data byte, STOP, each byte acknowledged. A read writes the command byte, then sends a repeated START and the address with R/W = 1; the part returns data bytes until the controller answers NACK and STOP. Reading the Input Port repeatedly gives fresh port data in each byte, and a read of the port clears INT without needing a STOP.

operation.topic: Pull-up resistors for SCL and SDA
operation.text: The lower limit on the pull-up comes from the supply, the allowed low level and the sink current; the upper limit from the allowed rise time and the bus capacitance. Bus capacitance, at most 400 pF, is the sum of this part's Ci (SCL) or Cio (SDA), the wiring and the other devices on the bus.

operation.topic: Supply current with LEDs on the port
operation.text: An LED from VCC to a port line leaves the pin about 1.2 V below VCC when off, and ΔICC grows as the pin falls below the supply. To save current, as on battery power, the pin is held at or above VCC while the LED is dark: by a high-value resistor across the LED, or by running the device from a supply at least 1.2 V below the LED supply.

The part is a target on the controller's I2C bus and sits near the lines it watches or drives. Usually VCCI is the lower controller supply and VCCP the higher one. Outputs drive enables, resets, power selects, switch gates and LEDs; inputs read interrupts, alarms, status lines and push buttons.

I2C speeds need no impedance control or differential routing. Avoid right-angle traces, spread signal traces apart as they leave the chip and widen power and ground traces. VCCP is bypassed with a larger capacitor for short supply dips and a smaller one for high-frequency ripple, both as close to the chip as possible; 0402 capacitors at VCCI and VCCP, each with a via to the ground plane, suit the TSSOP. Two layers work, signals on top and a split power and ground plane below; four layers with inner ground and power planes suit denser boards, with vias right beside the VCCI, VCCP and GND pads.
The exposed pad of the RGT package is soldered down; it carries heat and holds the part mechanically. Vias in it are optional; under paste they are filled, plugged or tented.
Latch-up immunity is above 100 mA (JESD 78, class II). The port shows no glitch at power-up.
